summary: Redwood walked Pathway through the Optimize console QProfile tools. Primary goal: understand where INT8 causes fidelity regressions vs FP8 and define a pilot to measure business impact. transcript:
[00:00] Marcus: hey everyone thanks for joining today uh we've got about an hour scheduled to go through the Optimize qprofile gap analysis, I'm Marcus from Redwood, AE on this account.
[00:08] Marcus: quick round robin? We'll just have people say name and role.
[00:12] Ellen: Ellen Park, Head of ML at Pathway Analytics.
[00:15] Ravi: Ravi Sharma, infra eng.
[00:17] Maya: Maya Torres, product.
[00:19] Priya: Priya Nair, solutions engineer — I'll drive the console demo.
[00:22] Marcus: great, thanks. High level: Pathway's been experimenting with our hosted API but wants to evaluate dedicated performance and qprofiles to hit latency SLOs without losing clinical fidelity in the extraction workflow. Today we show examples where int8 looks good almost everywhere but has corner-case drop offs vs fp8, and how Optimize helps you find and remediate that.
[00:42] Maya: quick context — we run a text-extraction pipeline for clinical notes, typical seq len 600 to 1,200 tokens, tail latency matters. Cost is sensitive but we can't tolerate hallucinations on key fields.
[00:56] Priya: perfect, that context helps. i'll share my screen now — opening Optimize console -> qprofiles -> heatmap. bear with me if the sharing lags.
[01:05] Priya: so this heatmap maps per-prompt fidelity delta between fp8 baseline and candidate int8 profiles; colors show relative BLEU/EM drop and confidence shifts. you'll see rows are prompt buckets (by intent and length) and columns are qprofile IDs.
[01:20] Ellen: mm-hmm I see — interesting that some short prompts have higher drop than mid-length ones, is that expected?
[01:27] Priya: yeah, sometimes quantization interacts with narrow context prompting and attention kernels, it can change token logits in ways that affect exact-match metrics. also, our auto-sensitivity sampler highlights outliers — those will be the ones we want to guard with fallbacks.
[01:41] Ravi: are these numbers from your internal corpus or simulated?
[01:44] Priya: this is demo data; when we run your sandbox we'll ingest your 1k prompts and run the same sweep. the console shows sample outputs and delta diffs — want me to open an example?
[01:54] Marcus: yes please show a few concrete examples so the team can understand the impact.
[01:58] Priya: okay opening sample prompt bucket A -> example 3. [02:03] Priya: fp8 output: "Patient reports intermittent chest pain since 04/21, no syncope." int8 output: "Patient reports chest pain 04/21, no episode noted." you can see small truncation and the date parsing shifted — that small difference would fail your downstream exact-match extraction.
[02:22] Ellen: that's the kind of failure we worry about — a missing 'intermittent' qualifier is material for our rules.
[02:27] Priya: exactly. Optimize can tag that prompt bucket as "sensitive" and create a fallback rule: for bucket A use fp8 qprofile or skip quantization. the console also suggests hybrid qprofiles where certain layers are kept higher precision.
[02:41] Marcus: quick note — when we say fp8 here, we mean Redwood-verified FP8 profile that keeps specific attention weights at fp8 while allowing other ops to remain lower precision; not all fp8 implementations are identical.
[02:53] Maya: what's the unit cost delta we should expect between int8 and that fp8 hybrid?
[02:57] Priya: ballpark — int8 can be 25–40% cheaper per token on our hosted fleet depending on sequence length and batching. the hybrid fp8 case is often 10–20% cheaper than full fp16/32 but more expensive than int8. we'll surface exact per-token cost in the sandbox and the console cost overlay.
[03:16] Ravi: latency — does fp8 materially change p99?
[03:19] Priya: good question. fp8 micro-op costs are usually similar to int8 for token generation, but fp8 hyperparameters and kernel choices can increase tail latency slightly. our platform gives latency percentiles per qprofile so you can compare 50/95/99 latencies.
[03:33] Priya: switching to the latency tab — here's a breakdown: int8 qprofile q-17 has median 48ms, p95 92ms, p99 230ms, hybrid-fp8 q-31 has median 55ms, p95 105ms, p99 280ms in this synthetic run. you can see p99 stretches a bit.
[03:51] Ellen: okay that p99 difference is meaningful for us, we try to cap at 300ms for the user-facing UI. but server-side async tasks can tolerate higher.
[03:58] Marcus: this is where routing and smart fallbacks help — you can route low-risk requests to int8 and high-risk to fp8 based on prompt classification, preserving SLA. the console supports policy routing by prompt tag.
[04:11] Maya: how do we generate those prompt tags? auto or manual?
[04:14] Priya: both. Optimize has an auto-sampler that clusters prompts by embedding and failure modes; you can also upload labeled prompts to seed the classifier.
[04:23] Ellen: walk me through the regression alerts — I want to be notified if production fidelity degrades after a qprofile rollout.
[04:28] Priya: sure. inside Alerts -> Quality, you set a baseline (we suggest current fp8 baseline) and tie alerts to metric thresholds (e.g., exact-match drop > 2% for any prompt set) and to specific prompt collections (like your extraction-critical set). alerts can trigger Slack/Email or create a policy to roll back.
[04:48] Marcus: we also support automatic canary rollouts where a small percent of traffic uses the new qprofile and we watch telemetry, then expand or rollback automatically if thresholds cross.
[04:58] Ravi: on the security side, how does the sandbox connect? we must meet SOC2 controls and route through our VPC.
[05:04] Priya: sandbox options: hosted isolated tenant with customer-managed KMS, or private deployment in your VPC. for the sandbox we usually do a VPC peering or private link plus IAM roles; we have SOC 2 Type II certs and can send the security pack. KMS/HSM integration is supported for Private deployments.
[05:21] Maya: what's the difference between dedicated and private for these tests?
[05:24] Marcus: dedicated is a reserved Redwood capacity with predictable throughput and isolation at the infra level; private is a deployment model where control plane sits in your VPC/on-prem and you manage networking and keys — private is heavier but required for some regulated data.
[05:36] Ellen: we may need private later but want to start with a sandbox in dedicated first to validate qprofiles.
[05:41] Priya: perfect. next I'll show the sensitivity sweep page — this is where we run int8/float8 mixes against your prompt set.
[05:48] Priya: launching a sweep demo: we vary layer-wise quantization and bitwidth, produce an accuracy curve vs latency curve. you can export the CSV and a decision report recommending candidate qprofiles with expected ROI.
[06:00] Priya: demo sweep shows a few candidate qprofiles: q-17 (aggressive int8), q-22 (mixed int8 with 2 layers fp16), q-31 (hybrid-fp8). the report flags two prompts with >10% EM drop on q-17.
[06:14] Ellen: curious — can we set a global fidelity SLA that blocks qprofiles that exceed a threshold?
[06:19] Priya: yes, the policy engine enforces global constraints: e.g., no qprofile with EM drop > 1% on your extraction-critical prompt set is allowed in auto-rollouts.
[06:29] Ravi: about telemetry — will we get token-level traces or just aggregated metrics?
[06:33] Priya: both. you get aggregated dashboards (latency, cost, accuracy) and can enable sampling to store token-level traces and KV cache snapshots for a small percent of requests to debug failures. those traces are redacted if you choose.
[06:47] Marcus: let's surface a concrete pilot plan — 30-day sandbox with 1k prompts, run int8/fp8 sweeps, produce decision report and recommended fallback rules, then a 2-week canary. does that sound right?
[07:00] Ellen: yes that works. question — do you have an automated rollback runbook if something slips into prod?
[07:05] Priya: we maintain a rollback playbook: immediate revert to prior qprofile, flush KV cache where necessary, and optionally switch to a more conservative batching profile to reduce tail. console shows a one-click rollback and an audit trail.
[07:17] Maya: audit logs — retention? we have compliance needs for 12 months.
[07:21] Marcus: we offer extended audit retention add-on; by default it's 90 days but enterprise packages can extend to 12+ months.
[07:29] Ravi: about cost modeling — can the console show forecasted monthly spend if we scale to 1M requests per month?
[07:34] Priya: yes the Cost overlay models per-hour cost by qprofile, accounts for batching efficiency and caching hit rates; you input traffic pattern and we simulate.
[07:44] Ellen: any gotchas we should be aware of with date parsing or extraction-specific heuristics?
[07:49] Priya: extraction often trips on subtle tokenization shifts; e.g., quantization can change logits around numeric tokens and separators. the Optimize sensitivity tool highlights token-level divergence heatmaps so you can target fixes — sometimes a layer-preserve hybrid fixes the issue without full fp8.
[08:05] Marcus: can we show how fallback routing looks in the console? Priya: yes opening routing -> policies.
[08:12] Priya: here's a policy: if prompt in "high-risk-extraction" tag, route to q-31 (fp8 hybrid); else route to q-17 (int8) with 5% randomized canary to q-31 for monitoring. you can also multiply backoffs or set latency caps.
[08:28] Maya: what about batch sizing — we need low latency, so aggressive batching could violate our UI SLO.
[08:33] Priya: batching is configurable per route; Optimize suggests batch target based on desired p99; you can enforce max batch wait or switch to single-request mode for UI paths.
[08:43] Ravi: does the rollout maintain K-V cache compatibility? if we fall back to fp8, do we lose cache hits and pay cost or is the cache portable?
[08:51] Priya: K-V cache layouts are compatible for compatible model variants; some qprofile changes require cache invalidation. Optimize flags when a qprofile will drop cache compatibility and suggests staged warm-ups to rebuild cache.
[09:05] Ellen: that's key for us because warm-up costs on long sequences are non-trivial.
[09:09] Priya: next — I'll show the decision report template. it includes: description of qprofiles tested, per-bucket delta table, recommended profile per bucket, expected cost delta, rollout plan (canary %, rollback triggers), and a notes section.
[09:23] Marcus: can Redwood run the initial sweep for Pathway or do you want us to run it in your sandbox?
[09:29] Ellen: we'd prefer Redwood runs it in our sandbox but we want results owned by us in a shared sheet.
[09:35] Priya: that's standard — we'll run under the sandbox tenant and export results to a shared Google Sheet we both have access to.
[09:41] Maya: timeline?
[09:43] Marcus: assuming we get the prompt set by Feb 6, Redwood will provision sandbox and run the sweep starting Feb 7, results by Feb 10, then sync and pick pilot start date.
[09:53] Ravi: security checklist — we need the SOC2 pack, SAML metadata for SSO, and contact for KMS onboarding.
[09:59] Marcus: i'll drop the SOC2 pack and SAML instructions in the CRM and loop in our security engineer. KMS onboarding contact will be in that email.
[10:07] Ellen: excellent. quick question on metrics — if we see a 0.5% EM drop but 30% cost savings, what's the recommended business decision?
[10:13] Marcus: depends on business tolerance and which fields are affected; Optimize can compute field-level risk and cost per field, so you can make an informed tradeoff. often teams accept small drops on non-critical fields while protecting critical ones.
[10:25] Priya: also remember you can do hybrid routing: int8 for general extraction, fp8 for named-entity fields.
[10:30] Maya: ok last bit — show me the export of the decision CSV.
[10:33] Priya: exporting now — columns: prompt_id, bucket, fp8_score, int8_score, delta, recommended_profile, expected_latency_ms. example row...
[10:44] [screen blips]
[10:47] Ellen: thanks that's very helpful. Are there any known edge-case models where int8 is actually better than fp8?
[10:52] Priya: rare, but depending on optimizer-kernel interactions some int8 kernels can be more stable for certain attention patterns; likely tool-specific. we'll surface those in the sweep.
[11:02] Marcus: ok, let's recap action items and next steps.
[11:06] Marcus: Ellen to share 1k prompt set and baseline metrics by Feb 6.
[11:09] Marcus: Priya to run sweep and post decision report by Feb 10.
[11:12] Marcus: Marcus to send sandbox access and security pack by Feb 4.
[11:15] Marcus: Ravi to confirm VPC peering needs and security POC by Feb 5.
[11:18] Ellen: sounds good. one more question — can you show a short simulated canary timeline?
[11:21] Priya: yes we can do 1% for 24h, look at prompt set alerts, then 10% for 48h, then 50% for a week, all gated by quantitative thresholds; the console automates that.
[11:33] Maya: perfect. thanks everyone.
[11:36] Marcus: thanks, we'll follow up with the invites and docs. meeting adjourned.
[11:41] [end recording]
